title: Find Everyday Information
creator: Original POC teaching demonstration (AI-assisted)
description: Use a fictional search interface to find an opening time, a price and a bus-arrival estimate.
learningObjective: Locate and select relevant information within a simple digital result card.
suggestedUse: Model an everyday need, then have the learner open the suitable practice screen and identify the requested detail.
adaptations: Reduce to one practice question.
Read the prompt aloud or pair with a visual cue.
Present fewer answer options.
Move from guided choices to independent searches on trusted real apps.
reusePermission: Adapt the original demonstration HTML for local teaching; review school policies, suitability and third-party contributions before redistributing.
curriculumContext: Illustrative digital literacy skill application; not an officially verified curriculum outcome mapping.
instructionalApproach: Model finding an appropriate app, scanning for a label and selecting the needed information.
assessmentCheck: Check whether the learner finds a new item and record prompts used.
transferTask: Find a current opening time or bus arrival with an educator on an approved real service.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use

title: Create and Save a Note
creator: Original POC teaching demonstration (AI-assisted)
description: Build a simple shopping list or reminder and save it to a temporary practice folder.
learningObjective: Create a short note, save it in a practice folder and reopen it.
suggestedUse: Practise selecting relevant items, saving the simulated note and opening it again.
adaptations: Reduce the number of choices.
Provide a first modelled example.
Use student-relevant, non-personal sample items.
Progress to editing a note in a real approved app.
reusePermission: Adapt the original demonstration HTML for local teaching; review school policies, suitability and third-party contributions before redistributing.
curriculumContext: Illustrative digital literacy skill application; not an officially verified curriculum outcome mapping.
instructionalApproach: Demonstrate create, review, save and reopen; fade each cue gradually.
assessmentCheck: Observe sequence completion and the support needed to find a saved note.
transferTask: Create and find a real classroom reminder in a school-approved notes application.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use

title: Digital Work Checklist
description: Navigate a fictional job app, open a task card and update a digital workplace checklist.
learningObjective: Navigate a simulated app to locate an assigned job and update completion status with appropriate prompting.
suggestedUse: Pair the digital checklist with a real stationery-packing task; ask the learner to open the correct job card and check off actual items packed.
adaptations: Use Guided mode before Independent mode, and record prompt levels.
Reduce the number of task steps or replace job descriptions with familiar school-based vocational tasks.
Allow pointing, touch access, keyboard or an appropriate access device; use real objects alongside the screen.
Do not equate tapping Done with completing the physical task: verify work separately.
creator: POC demonstration team
license: Original demonstration file; review before redistribution
curriculumContext: [Provisional] Vocational Education with digital literacy embedded: using a simulated digital checklist to support a familiar work process. Informed broadly by IMDA Digital Skills for Life (smart-device use). Not verified against a specific MOE SPED TLS or school Digital Literacy outcome.
instructionalApproach: Model opening a job app and checking a task card; then run guided practice with physical materials, fade cues, and revisit in a real task context.
assessmentCheck: Record whether the learner independently identifies the correct app, selects the intended job card, marks each completed step, and requests verification; record prompts separately from task accuracy.
transferTask: Use an approved digital checklist alongside a real school or vocational routine, with staff supervision and data-privacy checks.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — digital literacy / TLS alignment requires curriculum review

title: Device Care and Controls
creator: Original POC teaching demonstration (AI-assisted)
description: Use simulated Wi-Fi, volume, charging and screen controls to practise readiness and care.
learningObjective: Select and adjust appropriate device settings for a simple learning and care routine.
suggestedUse: Use the simulated tablet to prepare for a lesson and complete an end-of-lesson care routine.
adaptations: Begin with a single control.
Pair onscreen cues with the school’s actual devices.
Use a step-by-step visual checklist.
Adapt motor response requirements and provide more time.
reusePermission: Adapt the original demonstration HTML for local teaching; review school policies, suitability and third-party contributions before redistributing.
curriculumContext: Illustrative digital literacy skill application; not an officially verified curriculum outcome mapping.
instructionalApproach: Model the practical reason for each device control; rehearse the same cue on an approved real device.
assessmentCheck: Record correct settings and whether verbal, visual or physical support is required.
transferTask: Prepare a classroom tablet for an actual learning task following school procedures.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use

title: Check Before Sharing
creator: Original POC teaching demonstration (AI-assisted)
description: Choose safer next steps for fictional forwarded messages, prize links and online claims.
learningObjective: Pause and identify a trustworthy way to verify a claim before passing it on.
suggestedUse: Discuss short fictional posts, select a next action and explain why.
adaptations: Show one message at a time.
Use a read-aloud or visual explanation.
Reduce response options while teaching the same strategy.
Increase complexity only after demonstrating consistent understanding.
reusePermission: Adapt the original demonstration HTML for local teaching; review school policies, suitability and third-party contributions before redistributing.
curriculumContext: Illustrative digital literacy skill application; not an officially verified curriculum outcome mapping.
instructionalApproach: Model stopping to verify information with an official source or trusted adult.
assessmentCheck: Record whether the learner chooses an appropriate verification step and can transfer it to a new example.
transferTask: Practise checking a teacher-selected real digital claim before sharing with the class.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — requires educator review before classroom use

title: Workplace Message Practice
description: Practise selecting a recipient and a clear, relevant workplace message in a fictional chat app.
learningObjective: Select an appropriate recipient and functional message for a given workplace situation.
suggestedUse: Role-play a job update or help request after completing a supervised work task.
adaptations: Use Guided mode or reduce the number of messages to support earlier communicators.
Replace written phrases with learner-approved AAC symbols or personalised messages while preserving communication intent.
Model respectful, concise workplace communication with real communication partners.
Do not use learner phone numbers, staff contact lists, real chat accounts or identifiable personal information in this simulation.
creator: POC demonstration team
license: Original demonstration file; review before redistribution
curriculumContext: [Provisional] Communication and Language with possible Vocational Education application; broadly related to IMDA Digital Skills for Life (communicate online). Not a verified MOE SPED TLS learning-outcome mapping.
instructionalApproach: Model the situation, recipient and message choice, then practise supported selection; gradually vary contexts and reduce prompts. A message-selection simulation does not test spontaneous digital writing.
assessmentCheck: Across different scenarios, note correct recipient, relevance of message, prompting needed and ability to generalise the purpose of the communication.
transferTask: With appropriate permissions, practise sending a real workplace update through a school-approved channel to an agreed communication partner.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — digital literacy / TLS alignment requires curriculum review

title: Safe Online Choices
description: Choose safer responses to fictional situations involving private information, unexpected messages and respectful online behaviour.
learningObjective: Identify a safer response to basic online privacy and communication situations.
suggestedUse: Use each scenario as a starting point for teacher-guided discussion and rehearsal of asking for help.
adaptations: Read scenarios aloud and use concrete visuals or simplified language where necessary.
Offer two choices at a time and model what to do when unsure.
Practise the help-seeking response with a trusted adult or educator.
Avoid asking learners to enter or reveal actual passwords, ID numbers, contact details or school-account information.
creator: POC demonstration team
license: Original demonstration file; review before redistribution
curriculumContext: [Provisional] Digital safety in everyday living, broadly informed by IMDA Digital Skills for Life (be safe, smart and kind online). Daily Living Skills is a suggested discovery category, not a verified MOE SPED TLS mapping. [Provisional] The respectful online communication scenario may be a discussion starter for Healthy and Safe Relationships, but is not a verified HSR learning-outcome mapping.
instructionalApproach: Model a short decision routine: pause, keep information private, check with a trusted person, and communicate respectfully. Practise with supportive feedback and then novel examples.
assessmentCheck: Track the learner’s choice, explanation or help-seeking response across varied examples and the level of prompting required; do not treat repeated quiz answers as proof of real-world safety skills.
transferTask: During supervised real digital activities, rehearse seeking help before sharing information or responding to unexpected messages.
reviewStatus: Prototype demonstration — digital literacy / TLS alignment requires curriculum review
